 *     try token.permit(msg.sender, address(this), value, deadline, v, r, s) {} catch {}
 *     doThing(..., value);
 * }
 *
 * function doThing(..., uint256 value) public {
 *     token.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), value);
 *     ...
 * }
 * ```
 *
 * Observe that: 1) `msg.sender` is used as the owner, leaving no ambiguity as to the signer intent, and 2) the use of
 * `try/catch` allows the permit to fail and makes the code tolerant to frontrunning. (See also
 * {SafeERC20-safeTransferFrom}).
 *
 * Additionally, note that smart contract wallets (such as Argent or Safe) are not able to produce permit signatures, so
 * contracts should have entry points that don't rely on permit.
 */
interface IERC20Permit {
    /**
     * @dev Sets `value` as the allowance of `spender` over ``owner``'s tokens,
     * given ``owner``'s signed approval.
     *
     * IMPORTANT: The same issues {IERC20-approve} has related to transaction
     * ordering also apply here.
     *
     * Emits an {Approval} event.
     *
     * Requirements:
     *
     * - `spender` cannot be the zero address.
     * - `deadline` must be a timestamp in the future.
     * - `v`, `r` and `s` must be a valid `secp256k1` signature from `owner`
     * over the EIP712-formatted function arguments.
     * - the signature must use ``owner``'s current nonce (see {nonces}).
     *
     * For more information on the signature format, see the
     * https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2612#specification[relevant EIP
     * section].
     *
     * CAUTION: See Security Considerations above.
     */
    function permit(
        address owner,
        address spender,
        uint256 value,
        uint256 deadline,
        uint8 v,
        bytes32 r,
        bytes32 s
    ) external;

    /**
     * @dev Returns the current nonce for `owner`. This value must be
     * included whenever a signature is generated for {permit}.
     *
     * Every successful call to {permit} increases ``owner``'s nonce by one. This
     * prevents a signature from being used multiple times.
     */
    function nonces(address owner) external view returns (uint256);

    /**
     * @dev Returns the domain separator used in the encoding of the signature for {permit}, as defined by {EIP712}.
     */
    // solhint-disable-next-line func-name-mixedcase
    function DOMAIN_SEPARATOR() external view returns (bytes32);
}

owner().details: Returns the address of the current owner.

withdraw().details: This function transfers the withdrawable asset amount to the user and updates the totals. The function performs the following steps: 1. Checks if the user is allowed to withdraw their unlocked assets by calling `canWithdraw`. 2. Ensures that the funds are available for withdrawal by calling `fundsAvailable`. 3. Transfers the withdrawable asset amount from the contract to the user's address. 4. Updates the user's unlocked asset information and the total withdrawable asset amount. 5. Emits a `Withdraw` event with the user's address and the amount withdrawn.

params._backendAddress: The address of the backend, which is used for managing platform-specific operations.

constructor.details: This constructor sets the backend address for the contract.

params._shares: The number of shares to unlock. This represents the amount of shares the user wants to unlock from their total shares. If the user is the creator, they can only unlock after the strategy's expiration time. If the user is not the creator, they can unlock at any time. The shares must be less than or equal to the user's total shares minus any requested unlock shares.

unlock(uint256).details: This function processes the user's unlock request by updating the requested unlock shares and adding the user to the requestedUnlocks list. If the user has no pending unlock request, the user is added to the requestedUnlocks list.

params._enabled: A boolean value representing the new enabled status of the strategy. If set to true, the strategy will be enabled, allowing users to invest in it. If set to false, the strategy will be disabled, preventing new investments but allowing existing investments to be unlocked and withdrawn.

setEnabled(bool).details: This function allows the creator to enable or disable the strategy.If the strategy is disabled, users will not be able to invest in the strategy, but existing investments will remain active and will be available for unlocking and withdrawal.

setPremium(bool).details: This function allows the backend to update the premium strategy status.

params._user: The address of the user. If the user is the creator, they can only unlock after the strategy's expiration time. If the user is not the creator, they can unlock at any time.

canUnlock(address).details: This function determines if the user is allowed to unlock their shares based on the current time and the user's address.

returns.result: A boolean value indicating whether the user can unlock their shares. True if the user can unlock their shares, false otherwise.

renounceOwnership().details: Leaves the contract without owner. It will not be possible to call `onlyOwner` functions. Can only be called by the current owner. NOTE: Renouncing ownership will leave the contract without an owner, thereby disabling any functionality that is only available to the owner.

params._extendable: The new extendable status. If set to true, the strategy can be extended beyond its previous expiration time. If set to false, the strategy cannot be extended and will end at the expiration time set.

setExtendable(bool).details: This function allows the backend to update the extendable status of the strategy.

params._user: The address of the user requesting the withdrawal. This address is used to identify the user in the `userInfo` mapping and check their unlocked asset details.

canWithdraw(address).details: This function determines if the user is allowed to withdraw their unlocked assets based on the current block number and the user's unlocked asset amount.

returns.result: A boolean value indicating whether the user can withdraw their unlocked assets. True if the user can withdraw their unlocked assets, false otherwise.

params._assetAmount: The amount of the asset to convert to USD, specified in the smallest unit of the asset (e.g., wei for ETH).

getUsdValue(uint256).details: This function converts the given asset amount to its equivalent USD value based on the current asset price.

returns.usdValue: The USD value of the asset amount, calculated based on the current asset price from the Chainlink price feed.

params._id: The ID of the change log to retrieve. This ID corresponds to the index of the change log entry in the `changeLogs` mapping. The ID must be less than the total number of change logs (`changeLogsCount`).

getChangeLog(uint256).details: This function retrieves the change log details for a given ID.

returns.changeLog: The change log details, including block number, strategy change, cost in RAN, and price in RAN.

params._expiration: The new expiration time in seconds since the Unix epoch. This value represents the time at which the strategy will expire and no longer accept new investments. If the expiration time is extended beyond the current expiration and the strategy is not extendable, the transaction will revert.

setExpiration(uint256).details: This function updates the expiration time for the strategy, ensuring it is within the valid range.

params._user: The address of the user whose funds availability is being checked. This address is used to identify the user in the `userInfo` mapping and check their unlocked asset details.

fundsAvailable(address).details: This function determines if the user's unlocked assets are available for withdrawal based on the last update block and the user's next withdrawal allowed block.`totals.lastAvailUpdate` is the last block number when the strategy values were updated.      `user.unlocked.nextWithdrawalAllowed` is the block number after which the user can withdraw their unlocked assets.

returns.result: A boolean value indicating whether the funds are available for the user to withdraw. True if the funds are available, false otherwise.

params._amount: The amount of the asset that the user wants to invest in the strategy. This value represents the total amount of the asset that the user will transfer to the strategy.
params._referral: The address of the referral who referred the user to the strategy. This can be an address or zero address if no referral is involved. The referral address may be used for tracking and rewarding referrals.

invest(uint256,address).details: This function enables users to invest a specified amount of the asset into the strategy.

params._user: The address of the user for whom the profit information is being calculated. This address is used to identify the user in the `userInfo` mapping and retrieve their investment details.

getActualProfit(address).details: This function computes the profit, performance fees, and loss for a user's investment based on the current share price.

returns.profitInfo: A struct containing the profit information, including: - `assetInvestment`: The total amount of assets invested by the user. - `assetProfit`: The profit earned by the user from their investment. - `creatorPerformanceFee`: The performance fee allocated to the creator. - `platformPerformanceFee`: The performance fee allocated to the platform. - `assetLoss`: The loss incurred by the user from their investment. - `assetPriceUSD`: The current price of the asset in USD. - `withdrawableAssetAmount`: The amount of assets that the user can withdraw.

params._backendAddress: The new backend address. This address is used for managing platform-specific operations and has special permissions within the contract.

setBackendAddress(address).details: This function allows the backend to update the backend address used for managing platform-specific operations.

params._managedAddress: The new managed address. This is the address where trading operations happen and where the assets are stored.

setManagedAddress(address).details: This function allows the backend to update the managed address used for managing assets.

transferOwnership(address).details: Transfers ownership of the contract to a new account (`newOwner`). Can only be called by the current owner.

params._costRAN: The cost of the strategy in RAN tokens. This represents the amount of RAN tokens required to set or update the strategy.
params._checksum: The checksum of the strategy to ensure data integrity. This is a hash value used to verify that the strategy details have not been tampered with.
params._strategy: The strategy details in a compressed base64 encoded string. This string contains the encoded details of the strategy configuration.

setStrategy(string,uint256,bytes32).details: Records the strategy details in the change log by saving a compressed base64 encoded string sent by the backend.

params._userFees: The new user fees, including: - `depositFeeBP`: The deposit fee in basis points (1 basis point = 0.01%). - `performanceFeeBP`: The performance fee in basis points. - `ownerDepositFeeBP`: The owner deposit fee in basis points.

setUserFees((uint16,uint16,uint16)).details: This function allows the creator to update the fees that users will be charged for investing in the strategy.The `_userFees` parameter contains the deposit fee, performance fee, and owner deposit fee in basis points.

params._to: The recipient address to send the extracted tokens.
params._asset: The ERC20 token contract address of the asset to extract.
params._amount: The amount of tokens to extract and transfer.

extractToken(address,address,uint256).details: This function allows the backend to extract a specified amount of tokens from the contract and send them to a specified address.

params._availUpdate: A boolean indicating whether the funds in the smart contract have been updated.
params._operationsLimit: The maximum number of operations to process in a single call. 0 means no limit.
params._totalAssetAmount: The total amount of assets currently held in the strategy.

updateStrategyValues(uint256,bool,uint25.details: This function updates the total asset amount and share price, and handles requested investments and unlocks.

params._costRAN: The cost in RAN tokens for the strategy. This represents the amount of RAN tokens required to set or update the strategy.
params._checksum: The checksum of the strategy to ensure data integrity. This is a hash value used to verify that the strategy details have not been tampered with.
params._strategy: The strategy details in a compressed base64 encoded string. This string contains the encoded details of the strategy configuration.
params._initialDeposit: The initial deposit amount in the asset. This represents the amount of the asset that the creator initially deposits into the strategy.

initStrategy(string,uint256,bytes32,uint.details: This function sets the initial share price, processes the initial deposit, and records the strategy details.

params._times: The times for the strategy, including start time (timestamp), expiration time (timestamp), and last update block (block number).
params._userFees: The fees for the user, including deposit fee (in basis points), performance fee (in basis points), and owner deposit fee (in basis points).
params._rankFactory: The address of the RankFactory contract, which is responsible for creating and managing RankStrategy contracts.
params._creatorAddress: The address of the creator who will own and manage the strategy. This address will have special permissions within the contract.

initialize((uint16,uint16,uint16),(uint2.details: This function sets up the initial state of the contract, including fees, times, creator address, and rank factory address.

Independent grants, pauses and canonical calldata/value controls remain mandatory; zero native value required.

BNB Smart Chain56 RankStrategy Solady immutable-argument clones of0xf9b1859266b21dfc02c8bd31e11103f97a1aaffd; current runtime embeds that immutable delegate target and current official app selects their factory0x6e9d30690e433503d3db7001610f60290a286a3f. Factory and implementation source have Sourcify exact_match runtime/creation; clone identity uses observed eth_getCode plus full LibClone/Clone source, not a claimed independent exact_match record.

Both currently inventoried strategy epochs ended in April2026. invest requires enabled AND active epoch and is excluded; these are ordinary defined-maturity investor settlement methods, not evidence of project retirement or post-exploit recovery. Site/app still describe the own managed strategy product. No new investment or future epoch availability is promised.

unlock uses only msg.sender internal investment shares, a positive bounded share count and source ownership checks; creator may unlock only after expiration. After expiration the source replaces requested shares with ALL remaining unlockable shares, even if the caller supplied a smaller amount. Existing requested shares remain separately queued. No delegation, signature, caller-supplied receiver or arbitrary call data.

Unlock is asynchronous: backend updateStrategyValues processes requests and determines share price/NAV from supplied total assets; share accounting uses1e12 scale and floor rounding. Shares are internal ledger entries, not an ERC20 transferable token. Asset is BSC USDT0x55d398326f99059ff775485246999027b3197955 with18-decimal native amounts; principal is exposed to strategy profit/loss.

Profit conversion deducts creator performance fees and a platform fraction of those fees using basis-point arithmetic; source getActualProfit uses the mutable userFee schedule and Chainlink feed. No caller price minimum, payout minimum or deadline. Backend can change managed/backend addresses and extract tokens; no backend/admin/creator authority is admitted.

withdraw clears only msg.sender unlocked ledger and transfers its entire withdrawable amount to msg.sender. It requires canWithdraw and fundsAvailable: a later lastAvailUpdate block than unlock confirmation plus sufficient token balance. Maturity alone does not process an unlock or force funding. Assets are externally managed; backend processing and return of funds can delay/block settlement, with no timing or capital guarantee.
